hints: Focus on the class of each alcohol first, primary, secondary or tertiary, as this controls both oxidation and dehydration.
Recall that mild oxidation converts primary to aldehyde and secondary to ketone, but tertiary alcohols resist oxidation because there is no H on the C-OH carbon.
For cis-trans alkenes, look for which dehydration product gives a C=C with two different groups on each carbon, and check pent-2-ene versus pent-1-ene.
walkthrough:
**Classify X, Y and Z**

All three are $C_5H_{12}O$ isomers. Look at the carbon bearing the OH group.

$X = CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_2OH$ is primary, $Y = CH_3CH_2CH(OH)CH_2CH_3$ is secondary, $Z = (CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2CH_3$ is tertiary.

**Decide who reacts with mild oxidising agent**

Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes then acids, secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones.

$$RCH_2OH \xrightarrow{[O]} RCHO \xrightarrow{[O]} RCO_2H$$
$$R_2CHOH \xrightarrow{[O]} R_2C=O$$
Tertiary alcohols have no H on the C-OH carbon, so they do not react. Therefore only X and Y react.

**Decide who gives cis-trans $C_5H_{10}$ on dehydration**

Dehydration removes $H_2O$ to form an alkene. For cis-trans isomerism the C=C must have two different substituents on each carbon.

$Y$ (pentan-3-ol) dehydrates to pent-2-ene:
$$CH_3CH_2CH(OH)CH_2CH_3 \rightarrow CH_3CH_2CH=CHCH_3 + H_2O$$
Pent-2-ene exists as cis and trans forms. X gives pent-1-ene $CH_2=CHCH_2CH_2CH_3$ with two H on C1, so no cis-trans. Z gives $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$ with two $CH_3$ on one carbon, so no cis-trans. Therefore Y only gives the pair.

**Match to the row**

Reacts with mild oxidant: X and Y only. Gives cis/trans isomers: Y only. That combination is the correct row.

options.A: Incorrect because it claims X, Y and Z all oxidise. Z is tertiary $(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2CH_3$ with no H on the C-OH carbon, so it resists mild oxidation. This is a common trap of forgetting the selectivity of oxidation.
options.B: Incorrect on both columns. Z does not oxidise, and Z does not give cis-trans isomers. Dehydration of Z gives mainly 2-methylbut-2-ene $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$, which has identical $CH_3$ groups on one end of the double bond.
options.C: Correct. X (primary) and Y (secondary) are oxidised but Z (tertiary) is not. Only Y dehydrates to pent-2-ene $CH_3CH_2CH=CHCH_3$, which shows cis-trans isomerism, while X gives pent-1-ene and Z gives branched alkenes with no cis-trans forms.
options.D: Half right about oxidation (X and Y only) but wrong about dehydration. Z cannot give a cis-trans pair because its main alkene has two methyl groups on the same C=C carbon. It is Y, pentan-3-ol, that gives cis and trans pent-2-ene.
